Hi everyone! I am a masters student at UU and am a habitual lurker of Voat, ever since reddit had its exodus of users. I think its a great place to get news and insights into how people feel about the world. Provided that we remain skeptical of what influences those sources. It is refreshing to be a part of a new platform that still holds onto such ideals...well more than most.

I understand that one of the main reasons for the exodus from reddit was censorship, and lack of the ability to have a voice and freedom of speech. That leads me to a 2 part question.

Why did leave you reddit, if you were a user before and what was the final straw?
How important is freedom of speech on online platforms to you? If it is/is not, would you mind saying why?

Lastly, if you are bored and would like to expand more or go above and beyond on these subjects...I am thinking of working with and studying freedom of speech in the context of democracy and western culture. I have recently read about governments in western culture increasingly limiting freedom of speech. They cite reasons of rioting, racism, hate speech, and even terrorism type activity as justifications. I will not name the governments, nor the cases or politics behind such controversies. There are a vast amount of them, but I want to know how important is unburdening your identity towards being able to have a voice? Do you feel that you have a voice here? Do you think having a voice here leads to democracy? What kind of implications do online life have for democratic ideals? Feel free to expand, discuss or let me know what you feel. This is mostly a feeler for me as I plan to do much research outside of the voat realm, but am really interested in what you have to say. I find that these subjects are incredibly important for our society since the lines between online and offline life and identities are increasingly moving towards a blurry mirage.

I will also answer any questions you have for me, if you happen to have them and will be regularly checking back.

So hello! Thanks in advanced for your answers. :)

Freedom of speech on online platforms has its place. The Voat/Reddit style is where freedom of speech really has its chance to shine. Everyone has the ability to say what they want and the better supported opinions and facts will rise up to the top. Overall it's just kind of a balance just like everything else. Censorship has benevolent uses, but people need to err more on the side of freedom of speech.
